Itza Maya

Itza’ Maya language and community work in San José, Petén, is documented through educational publications and named collaborations. Read the community’s own teaching materials alongside an older linguistic report, keeping contemporary identity distinct from language fluency and historical kingdoms.

Read the sources [1] Comunidad Lingüística Itza’, ALMG; translator Herbert Marcony Chayax Tesucún [3] Charles Andrew Hofling; FAMSI, Spanish translation Alex Lomónaco

01

Identity and homelands

The Itza’ linguistic community’s institutional home is San José, Petén, within the contemporary Maya world of northern Guatemala.

Read the sources [1] Comunidad Lingüística Itza’, ALMG; translator Herbert Marcony Chayax Tesucún

02

Historical context

ALMG publishes Maya Itza’ literature and language materials; these are useful sources for studying continuity beyond archaeological accounts of ancient Maya cities.

Read the sources [1] Comunidad Lingüística Itza’, ALMG; translator Herbert Marcony Chayax Tesucún

03

Living communities and further study

In October 2026, San José reported completion of a two-year teacher-training program coordinated with ALMG to strengthen Maya Itza’ teaching.

Read the sources [2] Municipalidad de San José, Petén

04

Community-produced teaching materials

The 2022 ALMG book identifies the Itza’ linguistic community in San José and explains its aim of strengthening children’s learning. Its teacher introduction discusses Itza’ as a second language for pupils whose first language is Spanish. That context shows why language use cannot function as a simple test of community identity.

Read the sources [1] Comunidad Lingüística Itza’, ALMG; translator Herbert Marcony Chayax Tesucún

05

A named language collaborator

Hofling’s report credits Félix Fernando Tesucún’s contributions to documentation and explains his decision to study one speaker’s language in depth. The publicly linked report supplies selected front matter, not the entire published grammar. Its1998 research conditions and historical speaker estimates are not current counts.

Read the sources [3] Charles Andrew Hofling; FAMSI, Spanish translation Alex Lomónaco

06

A dated teacher-training account

San José’s October2026 municipal report describes a two-year training programme involving teachers from San José and San Andrés, ALMG’s Itza’ linguistic community and education authorities. This is a reported educational activity; its stated hopes do not establish measured learning outcomes.

Read the sources [2] Municipalidad de San José, Petén

What needs further research

  • Add independently corroborated histories of Noj Petén, colonial change and present communities.
  • Seek fuller Itza’-authored publications and outcomes evidence for language programmes.
